strongest_angle: Companies that replaced workers with AI are facing a 19 percent rebound rate in the United States, forcing employers to re-hire laid-off staff who demand higher pay and job security.

key_facts.fact: In a survey of U.S. workers conducted by Propeller Insights for SHL, 19 percent of respondents replaced by AI were later asked to return to their jobs.
In the United Kingdom, 13 percent of surveyed workers who were replaced by AI reported being asked back by their original employer.
Across both the United States and the United Kingdom combined, 16 percent of surveyed workers were replaced by AI and subsequently asked to return.
Market research firm Propeller Insights polled over 1,000 U.S. workers and over 1,000 U.K. workers for talent management company SHL.
According to research released by SHL in London, more than 33 percent of workers have experienced AI displacement firsthand or know someone who has.
Fortune reporter Joshua Hong documented on November 9, 2026, that returning U.S. workers replaced by AI are demanding higher pay, job security, and AI transparency.
The Globe and Mail writer Déjà Leonard reported on October 25, 2026, that U.S. workers are asked back at a rate of 19 percent compared to 13 percent for U.K. workers.
CNBC reporter Sophie Caldwell reported on October 30, 2026, that AI-driven layoffs created a new class of boomerang employees returning to former employers.
